summary: The revision is more honest and cheaper, but demand is still unproven. The new Art. 14(8) hook covers only actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents, not routine not_affected triage, so the paid driver is downstream OEM requests nobody has evidenced. Narrowing to Yocto makers running Dependency-Track also shrinks an already unsized market.

objections.objection: The repositioned compliance hook does not carry the product. Art. 14(8) requires informing users, 'where appropriate' in machine-readable form, only after the manufacturer becomes aware of an actively exploited vulnerability or severe incident. That is a rare event for a mid-size maker and is a notification duty, not a duty to publish per-release not_affected VEX across all findings. The bulk of VEXpath's value (noise cut, cross-release ledger) has no regulatory pull; it relies on OEM customer demand that the evidence does not show.

Demand evidence is unchanged: developer GitHub issues (engagement 1-43), some from open-source maintainers with no budget, and none from a Yocto device maker's PSIRT or CRA owner. The revision admits this in risks and moves the burden to the riskiest-assumption test, which is right, but until that test runs there is no sign of budgeted pain in the named segment.

The narrowing compounds the size problem. The buyer now has to be an EU maker with 50-1,000 staff, firmware on Yocto/embedded Linux, already producing SBOMs, already running Dependency-Track or OE cve-check, and with a named CRA owner. Each filter cuts the pool; the concept itself guesses 'a few thousand' for a broader profile with no source. At EUR 3.5k ACV, even 300 customers is about EUR 1M ARR, so the segment may not support a venture-scale company.

Budget competition inside the CRA stack. CVD Portal sells Art. 14 reporting plus SBOM management, remediation tracking and CSAF advisories from EUR 1,188-3,588/yr, grant-eligible. VEXpath at EUR 3,480/yr roughly doubles a mid-size maker's CRA tooling spend for one sub-step that the suite already lists. Buyers who must justify spend to a regulatory or quality manager will likely accept the suite's manual VEX first.

Urgency remains deadline-shaped: main obligations land 11 December 2027 and the revision left this unchanged. Expect thin 2027 revenue and a buying spike late in 2027, which a seed company must survive on design-partner income.

strongest_point: Binding CRA dates plus a cheap, self-hosted, DT-native add-on aimed at embedded makers the enterprise SBOM vendors ignore; the test now asks for paid LOIs and a named approver.
what_would_change_my_mind: At least 4 of 15 CRA owners at 50-500-person EU Yocto device makers sign a EUR 290/month LOI with a named spend approver (the concept's own test).
At least 8 of 15 can show a written VEX or vulnerability-status request from a downstream OEM or operator in the last 12 months.
A sourced count (industry-association or Yocto/DT community data) of at least 2,000 EU makers matching the narrowed profile.
A CRA suite (CVD Portal, sbomify) agrees to resell or bundle the engine, showing a channel that reaches buyers at this ACV.
A draft harmonised standard or market surveillance guidance that expects VEX/CSAF for routine vulnerability handling.

resolved_prior.objection: Demand evidence is developer GitHub issues, not purchase intent from the named buyer.
resolved_prior.note: Evidence unchanged; acknowledged in risks and the test now requires LOIs and a named approver, which is the right fix but not yet run.

resolved_prior.objection: Compliance hook weaker than pitched: CRA mandates neither VEX nor CSAF.
resolved_prior.note: Overclaim removed, which is good, but the replacement hook (Art. 14(8)) only covers actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents, so routine triage still lacks regulatory pull.
Not changed by design; lower price and product-led motion reduce burn per deal but not the timing.

resolved_prior.objection: WTP evidence comes from enterprise contracts and sbomify anchors prices low.
resolved_prior.note: Price cut to EUR 3,480/yr and framed as an add-on beside suites; enterprise comparables kept as ceiling; WTP is now tested directly. Budget competition with suites remains (new objection).

resolved_prior.objection: CSAF matching may be commoditised in Dependency-Track.
resolved_prior.note: Core moved to Yocto build evidence, invalidation and signing; DT's CSAF matching becomes an input.

resolved_prior.objection: Market size for the exact profile is unquantified.
resolved_prior.note: Added as an open question, but the narrowed profile makes the pool smaller and it is still unsourced.
